items.title: Alpiq to Acquire 90% of Harmony Energy
items.summary: Switzerland-based power firm Alpiq is buying a 90% stake in UK battery storage developer-operator Harmony Energy, consolidating its position in the European BESS market. The deal underscores continued European consolidation among storage developers and operators.

items.title: Frontier Power Secures Four BESS Projects From Stella
items.summary: Long-duration storage developer Frontier Power USA has exercised an exclusive selection right to acquire four battery storage projects from clean energy platform Stella Energy Solutions. The move expands Frontier's pipeline of US storage assets as it builds out its long-duration portfolio.

items.title: Victoria and Energy Dome to Build First State LDES Plant
items.summary: Victoria's State Electricity Commission has partnered with Italian clean-tech firm Energy Dome to develop the Australian state's first long-duration energy storage facility. The project marks a step toward diversifying Australia's storage mix beyond lithium-ion.

items.title: Palau Hybrid Project Gets 19.8MWh Battery Expansion
items.summary: A 19.8MWh battery energy storage system is being added to an existing solar-plus-storage facility in Palau, backed by Australian development finance. The expansion strengthens one of the Western Pacific's flagship hybrid renewable projects.

items.title: Chinese Integrators Hold 76% of Global BESS Market
items.summary: Chinese system integrators cemented their dominance of the global battery energy storage market, capturing 76% share worldwide in 2025. The figure highlights the scale of China's lead over Western and other Asian competitors in system integration.

items.title: Scientists Crack Solid-State Battery Dendrite Mystery
items.summary: Researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials have identified the mechanical fracture mechanism by which soft lithium dendrites crack the hard ceramic electrolyte inside solid-state batteries, causing short circuits. The finding, publicized this week, could help engineers design safer, longer-lasting cells for EVs and electronics.

items.title: China Set to Release First Solid-State Battery Standard
items.summary: China is finalizing its first national standard defining terminology and classification for solid-state electric vehicle batteries, expected for release this month. The standard aims to bring clarity to a market crowded with competing 'solid-state' claims from automakers, most of which are actually semi-solid designs.

items.title: HyperStrong to Launch Sodium-Ion BESS in China First
items.summary: System integrator HyperStrong plans to deploy sodium-ion battery energy storage systems first in its home market of China before bringing the product internationally, according to its technology president. The staged rollout reflects a broader industry push toward non-lithium chemistries for grid storage.

items.title: Eni Storage Breaks Ground on Italian LFP Gigafactory
items.summary: Eni Storage Systems has broken ground on a gigafactory in Italy that will build lithium iron phosphate cells for energy storage applications. Separately, Chinese firm Hithium won an 80 million euro grant from the Spanish government for a battery and BESS plant.

items.title: Peak Energy, ESS Tech Advance Sodium-Ion Storage Push
items.summary: Peak Energy, ESS Tech and Unigrid have each made fresh announcements advancing sodium-ion energy storage technology across US and European markets. The moves add to growing momentum for alternative chemistries as developers seek to diversify away from lithium supply chains.

items.title: FERC Orders Six Grid Operators to Justify Large-Load Tariffs
items.summary: FERC issued tailored show-cause orders to all six major RTOs/ISOs, directing them to justify or reform tariffs governing how data centers and other large loads, including co-located battery storage, connect to the grid. Each operator has 60 days to defend existing rules or propose changes covering transmission cost allocation and co-location arrangements.

items.title: ISO-NE Seeks Delay on FERC Large-Load Tariff Reform
items.summary: ISO-NE and regional transmission owners announced intent to request a 90-day abeyance in FERC's large-load show-cause proceeding covering data center and co-located load tariff reforms. The delay would allow a stakeholder process ahead of a November 16, 2026 filing deadline.

items.title: New Jersey Signs Transmission Cost and Data Center Tariff Bills
items.summary: New Jersey's governor signed legislation aimed at cutting transmission owners' allowed return on equity, establishing new data center tariffs, and requiring state approval for supplementary transmission projects. The bills respond to rising ratepayer concerns tied to large-load and storage-related grid buildouts.

items.title: EU Draft Plan Calls for 200GW of Storage by 2030
items.summary: A leaked draft of the European Union's Electrification Action Plan states the bloc must deploy 200GW of energy storage by 2030 to meet flexibility needs on its grid. The target signals a significant policy push for storage buildout across member states.
